issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Ad-hoc "Log activity": removing ONE logged activity silently deletes EVERY same-named activity that day (data loss). The new sheet's Remove (X) and the plan tick-off both delete by name+date, but log always inserts a new row.

Root cause (frontend + backend):
- Remove passes the NAME, not the row id: src/components/activity/LogActivitySheet.tsx:327 -> removeMut.mutate(entry.activity_name) -> loggingService.unlogActivity({activity_name, log_date}) (logging.service.ts:104).
- Backend DELETE /api/logs/activity deletes ALL rows matching user+date+lower(name): app/routes/logging.py:1228-1230 (.delete(synchronize_session=False), no id, no LIMIT 1). Returns {deleted: N}.
- POST always INSERTs a fresh row (logging.py:1191-1202, no upsert/dedup). No unique constraint on (name,date) — db_models.py ActivityLog has only a NON-unique idx_activity_log_user_date. So two same-name rows/day are allowed and each renders as its own <li key={entry.id}> (LogActivitySheet.tsx:303).
- Same by-name delete is used by the plan tick-off: src/components/activity/ActivityMarkSection.tsx:101 unlogActivityMut.mutate({activity_name: activity.name, log_date}).

Repro (single feature):
1. /activity -> Log activity -> type Cardio, Name "Run", Duration 30 -> Save.
2. Log activity again -> Name "Run", Duration 20 -> Save.
3. Reopen the sheet: both "Run" entries show under "Also logged today".
4. Tap X on the 20-min Run. Toast: "removed".
Expected: only that one entry is removed.
Actual: BOTH Run rows are deleted (DELETE returns {deleted:2}); the 30-min run and its data are destroyed silently.

Repro (cross-feature, worse — the ad-hoc row is invisible):
1. Plan has activity target "Morning Walk"; user also logs an ad-hoc "Morning Walk" via the sheet (hidden from the sheet list because it matches a plan name).
2. Plan "Morning Walk" now shows completed (backend marks a plan activity done when ANY same-name ActivityLog exists). User un-ticks it in ActivityMarkSection.
Actual: the ad-hoc Morning Walk is deleted too, with no indication.

Fix: delete by ActivityLog.id scoped to the user (add id to unlogActivity + the row), not by name. Plan tick-off (which legitimately keys on name) should delete only the most-recent matching row or tag plan-generated logs so it never touches ad-hoc rows. Verified: tsc clean; both repos traced; adversarial verify CONFIRMED all 6 links, no unique constraint.

fix.description: Root cause: buildRestCue (src/pages/Activity.tsx) had no final-set guard and framed the just-logged reps as the next set's Target. After the last set of a 3-set exercise it spoke a phantom 'set 4 of 3', and on an under-target set it mis-coached the low reps as the target. Fix: extracted to src/lib/restCue.ts (pure) - returns undefined when nextSet > target_sets (RestTimer then skips speech), and the Target line now reads the plan's prescribed reps from current_target (e.g. '3x8-10' -> '8 to 10'), not the reps just logged. Proof: voice/audio-only behavior with no visual surface (cue fires only after logging the final set of a LIVE workout; screenshot shows the correct /activity route on a rest day). Verified by new unit test test/restCue.test.ts (6/6 green) covering final-set suppression + prescribed-vs-logged reps.

judge.note: Root-caused to buildRestCue; both reported defects fixed (final-set suppression + prescribed-reps target); unit-tested 6/6; tsc clean; minimal surgical scope. Non-visual voice bug so proof is the test + affected-route screenshot.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Voice rest-timer cue announces a phantom "set N+1 of N" after the FINAL set, contradicting the on-screen "Workout complete"/"Next up", and mislabels the just-completed set's reps/weight as the next set's "Target". New voice-cues feature (commit b7df14c5), opt-in (Profile > Voice cues) + Sounds on.

Root cause (src/pages/Activity.tsx):
- The rest timer arms after EVERY logged set while the picker is open, with NO final-set guard: logSetMutation.onSuccess sets lastLoggedSetRef then, if isModalOpen.current, restarts the timer (Activity.tsx:515-533).
- buildRestCue always computes nextSet = (lastSet.set_number ?? 0)+1 and appends " of {target_sets}" (Activity.tsx:57-59). After logging the last set of a 3-set exercise: lastLoggedSet=3 -> nextSet=4, total=3 -> "set 4 of 3".
- The cue is spoken by RestTimer's completion effect (RestTimer.tsx:51 speakRestCue(announceOnComplete)) after the rest duration elapses.
- Secondary (same root): the "Target {reps} reps at {kg} kilos" line (Activity.tsx:60-61) uses lastLoggedSetRef — the set JUST COMPLETED — but frames it as the upcoming set's TARGET, ignoring the plan's prescribed target (currentExercise.current_target). On a failed/under-target set (did 5 of a 10 target) it announces "Target 5 reps" — mis-coaching.

Repro:
1. Profile > Preferences: Sounds ON, Voice cues ON.
2. /activity -> start a live workout -> open a 3-set exercise -> log set 3/3. Do NOT tap Continue/Finish; pocket the phone.
3. After the 90s rest, the phone says: "Rest over. Next: <exercise>, set 4 of 3. Target <last reps> at <last kg> kilos."
Expected: no cue after the last set (or announce the real next exercise / prescribed target).
Actual: phantom set "4 of 3"; if a next exercise exists the screen says "Next up: Squats" while the voice says the finished exercise "set 4 of 3" (double-wrong). Distinct from fixed 2ea5 (that was workout-completion detection, not the spoken cue).

Fix: suppress the cue when nextSet > target_sets (final set), and base the "Target" line on the plan's prescribed next-set target rather than lastLoggedSetRef.

[bug-hunt] Ad-hoc "Log activity" sheet's "Also logged today" list is sourced from ALL of today's activity_logs (not just entries the sheet created), so it surfaces rows it cannot manage: (a) nameless AI-coach-logged rows show with a permanently-disabled Remove X, and (b) a legit ad-hoc entry whose name collides with a plan activity is filtered out entirely — logged and counted toward streak/calories, but invisible and un-removable.

- (a) AI coach activity_logger blocks store rows with activity_name = NULL when the canonical type equals the activity type: src/lib/block-transformers.ts:186 (activity_name: activity?.type !== activityType ? activity?.type : undefined) -> useBlockSubmit.ts logActivity -> NULL name. In the sheet that row renders (name falls back to the type label, :310) but Remove is disabled={... || !entry.activity_name} (:329) and the handler is guarded if(entry.activity_name) (:327), and backend requires a name (logging.py:1226). => visible entry with a dead X, un-removable through any UI.

issues.description:
[suggestion] Goal ETA — a calm "On track for <date>" line on the Log Weight screen that projects when you will actually reach your goal weight at your CURRENT logged pace.

User problem: the single most-asked question of anyone cutting or bulking — "given how I am actually trending, when do I hit my goal?" — is the one thing the app never answers. Log Weight already shows the past trend + observed rate (e.g. -0.4 kg/wk) and, separately, the kg remaining, but never combines them. The only forward projection in the app (WeeklyTrajectory on Plan Timeline/onboarding) uses the PLAN prescribed pace in "weeks", not the user real measured rate — so an off-plan lifter gets a fantasy timeline, not reality.

Evidence: observed EWMA weekly rate (ratePerWeek, LogWeight.tsx:391-406) and remaining kg (goalProgress.remaining, LogWeight.tsx:336) are BOTH already computed on this exact screen and rendered as separate stats — nothing divides one into the other to yield a date (grepped: no ETA/projected-date logic in LogWeight.tsx). The plan-pace projection (src/lib/weekly-projection.ts / WeeklyTrajectory) is a different, plan-based, week-indexed forecast on a different screen. Competitors (HealthifyMe et al.) surface goal-date estimates; NYUS has the data but does not show it.

Proposed v1: one card/line on /log-weight — "At your current pace (-0.4 kg/wk) you will reach your 75 kg goal around 14 Sep · ~11 weeks." Frontend-only, reuses the existing rate + remaining. Guard rails (fits the precision-over-encouragement brand): require >=3 logged points, and if the user is stalled or trending AWAY from goal, show "Not trending toward your goal yet — keep logging" instead of a fake date. Label it an estimate, like weekly-projection.ts already does. No backend.

Rough effort: S (~1-2 frontend files: a small pure helper + a card in LogWeight.tsx; data already present).

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Weekly Review: the AI's proposed plan changes NEVER render (approve/modify flow is dead), the Insights tab is always empty, and the protein target always shows "/ 0g" — all rooted in the /reviews serializer. Real users can never see or approve the coach's weekly plan adjustments.

Root cause (backend app/routes/reviews.py::_serialize_review + frontend src/services/review.service.ts::normalizeReview).

1) PROPOSED CHANGES (HIGH — core feature dead): db_models.py:1734 declares `proposed_changes = db.Column(JSON)`, but the engine writes it as a STRING via `review.proposed_changes = json.dumps(proposed_changes)` (app/services/weekly_review.py:534) and reads it back with `json.loads(review.proposed_changes)` everywhere (weekly_review.py:653/857, scheduler_jobs.py:627) — proving the attribute is a JSON string. `_serialize_review` (reviews.py:57) returns `r.proposed_changes` WITHOUT json.loads, so the API sends proposed_changes as a JSON string e.g. "[{...}]". FE normalizeReview (review.service.ts:46) only handles an Array or an {adjustments:[...]} object: Array.isArray(string) is false and string.adjustments is undefined -> `?? []`. proposed_changes collapses to []. PlanDiffViewer shows "No plan changes proposed this week" and the primary CTA is disabled ("Select changes to approve"); the user can only Keep Current / Discuss. Secondary: even if the string were parsed, the engine's per-change shape is {category, current_value, proposed_value, reason} — no id/label and different key names than the FE's {id, field, label, current, proposed} — so cards would render blank and selection (keyed on change.id) would break; the {adjustments:{type,from,to,target}} branch matches a shape the engine never emits. Masked in QA only because dev ?demo=1 (WeeklyReviewScreen.tsx:241-322) injects a proper array.

2) INSIGHTS (MED): _serialize_review emits NO top-level `insights` field (getById returns none; /latest only nests them under data.adjustment.insights, which the FE never reads). FE `insights: raw.insights ?? []` (review.service.ts:51) -> always []. The AI Insights section reads "No notable patterns this week." on every real review.

3) PROTEIN TARGET (MED): the model has target_daily_protein (set weekly_review.py:516) but _serialize_review omits it (and target_daily_steps). FE `protein_target: raw.target_daily_protein ?? 0` (review.service.ts:56) -> 0. The Overview chip renders "{avg_protein}g / 0g" on every real review (calorie target + meals serialize fine; protein target uniquely does not).

Repro: open /weekly-review for a user with a real generated review (NOT ?demo=1). Overview shows "Ng / 0g" protein; Insights tab shows "No notable patterns this week"; Plan Changes shows "No plan changes proposed" with the approve CTA disabled — even though the AI generated proposed changes + insights.

Expected: proposed changes render as selectable diff cards with a working Approve / Approve-N-of-M; Insights shows the week's detected patterns; protein target shows the real value (e.g. "158g / 160g").

Fix (all in _serialize_review, one place): json.loads(proposed_changes) before returning and normalize each item to {id, field/category, label, current, proposed, reason} (OR relax normalizeReview to JSON.parse a string + map the engine's current_value/proposed_value keys); add a top-level `insights`; add target_daily_protein + target_daily_steps. Re-QA the approve/modify/reject round-trip after the fix.
issues.reviewReason: Fixed + pushed + DEPLOYED (frontend commit 820566e9, backend commit f052a5d, prod restarted + healthy). Root cause: backend _serialize_review returned proposed_changes raw, but it is stored as a json.dumps string of engine items {category,current_value,proposed_value}; the FE collapsed the string to [] so the approve/modify flow was dead. It also omitted a top-level insights field and target_daily_protein/steps, so Insights always read No notable patterns and protein showed slash 0g. Fix: backend now json.loads + reshapes proposed_changes to the FE contract, emits insights (with id + pattern_tag) and target_daily_protein/steps; FE normalizeReview also parses a string + maps engine keys idempotently as a safety net. Verified: 22 FE unit tests pass (new regression tests included), tsc clean, and I ran the deployed normalizers on prod - they emit the exact FE shape (protein maps to macros, calories to calories, numerics kept, None and bad-string to []). Full on-screen render still needs a user with a real generated weekly review (QA account has none; not provisioning per your directive). Safe to Resolve after you open a real weekly review on-device.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Monthly Progress: the "Nothing logged yet" onboarding empty state is UNREACHABLE, so a brand-new / no-data user sees a dashboard full of confusing zeros ("0 / N activities done", 0d streaks) instead of the intended first-run empty state. Same root also mislabels the hero ring's denominator.

Root cause (src/pages/MonthlyProgress.tsx + backend backend.py monthly-progress endpoint).
- The whole-month empty-state guard `hasAnyMonthlyData` (MonthlyProgress.tsx:299-309) OR-includes `activitiesTotal > 0` (line 303), where `activitiesTotal = progressData?.activities_done?.total ?? 0` (line 287). But the backend sets `activities_done.total = days_elapsed` (backend.py:5410) and `days_elapsed = (today - start_of_month).days + 1` (backend.py:5248) — ALWAYS >= 1 (even on the 1st of the month). So `activitiesTotal > 0` is unconditionally true on any successfully-loaded response -> hasAnyMonthlyData is always true -> the empty branch (onboarding illustration + "Log a meal / Start a workout" CTAs, gated at line 465) is DEAD CODE for real users.
- Same root hits the hero ring: with no workout plan (sessionsTotal===0) it falls to the `activitiesTotal > 0` branch (line 335) and renders `activitiesCompleted / activitiesTotal` captioned "activities done", where activitiesCompleted = count of days with a completed activity (backend.py:5297) and the denominator is days-into-the-month. So the user sees e.g. "3 / 11 activities done · 27% this month" where 11 is merely the day-of-month, not a planned-activity count. The intended "days logged / days-in-month" fallback (line 344) is therefore also dead code.

Repro: brand-new account (no plan, no meal/workout/weight logs, no streaks) -> open Progress -> Monthly (/monthly-progress).
Expected: the "Nothing logged yet" first-run empty state with the log CTAs.
Actual: the full dashboard renders — hero ring "0 / N activities done" (N = days elapsed), "No sessions scheduled this month", "No meal plan yet", 0d streaks — exactly the confusing state the empty branch was built to prevent.

Fix: drop activitiesTotal (and activitiesCompleted) from the hasAnyMonthlyData guard — they are derived from days-elapsed, not real logs, and daysLogged/anyDayLogged already covers genuine activity; and either relabel the hero "activities" ring or base it on daysLogged/monthDayCount so the denominator is meaningful.
issues.reviewReason: Fixed + pushed (frontend commit ba58dd56). Root cause: MonthlyProgress hasAnyMonthlyData OR-included activitiesTotal/activitiesCompleted, which the backend derives from days-elapsed (activities_done.total = days_elapsed, always >= 1), so the guard was always true and the Nothing logged yet first-run empty state was dead code; the hero ring also showed a meaningless N of day-of-month activities done. Fix: dropped those two day-derived values from the guard (genuine activity is still covered by anyDayLogged) and removed the hero ring activities branch so it falls to daysLogged/monthDayCount (days logged). Verified: tsc clean. Seeing the empty state needs a brand-new no-data account. Safe to Resolve after an on-device check with a fresh account.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Plan-independent food diary shows "0 kcal logged" for the DEFAULT free-text log — the new feature's headline running-totals card is dead on its own primary path.

The no-plan food diary (commit e6f84228, closes i-20260711-fdry) renders a "Today's food diary" card with a big kcal headline + P/C/F macro tiles + per-item list, for users with NO AI diet plan who track home-cooked food. Its primary CTA "Log what you ate" (NutritionDiaryCard.tsx:102 / NutritionEmptyState.tsx:44 / Nutrition.tsx:481) opens CustomMealModal, which DEFAULTS to the 'quick' free-text tab (CustomMealModal.tsx:60 useState('quick')).

A plain typed log attaches macros ONLY when a prior photo-analysis description still matches the text (CustomMealModal.tsx:351-358); text typed from scratch => macros=null => POST /logs/meal with no total_calories/protein/carbs/fat (CustomMealModal.tsx:360-366). Backend log_meal stores total_calories=body.get('total_calories') = NULL with ZERO server-side estimation (nyu_backend app/routes/logging.py:803-806). getDailyLogs serializes those nulls; the diary sums m.total_calories ?? 0 (Nutrition.tsx:320-325) => 0.

Result: the exact target user (home-cooked tracker, no plan) who taps the primary CTA and types their meal gets a diary whose flagship metric is uniformly ZERO — headline "0 kcal logged" (NutritionDiaryCard.tsx:54-57) and every item "0 kcal · P0g C0g F0g" (:88, :93). Only the item name + count are correct. The macro-bearing paths are all non-default/gated: photo analysis is Pro-only (403/429 for free users), the Ingredients tab needs a tab-switch + search, and re-logging a recent free-text meal carries null again.

Repro:
1. Account with NO AI diet plan -> /nutrition.
2. Tap "Log what you ate" -> stays on Quick Log tab -> type "2 roti, 1 katori dal" -> Log Meal.
3. Reopen /nutrition.
Expected: diary reflects the meal with an estimated/entered kcal + macros (or prompts to add them).
Actual: "Today's food diary · 1 item · 0 kcal logged"; item shows "0 kcal · P0g C0g F0g" — the running-totals card looks broken on its own primary flow.

Fix options: (a) let the free-text quick log capture optional kcal/macros inline (like the Ingredients "Add new" form) so a text meal can carry numbers; (b) route free text through the AI macro estimator for ALL users (or a cheap heuristic) before logging; (c) when a meal truly has no macros, show a per-item "No calories entered — add them" and SUPPRESS the 0-kcal headline instead of asserting a false "0 kcal logged" total.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Food logged via the new no-plan food diary is invisible on the DASHBOARD diet card — it still says "no diet plan", contradicting the diary the user just filled.

The plan-independent food diary (commit e6f84228) makes no-plan meal logging first-class: /nutrition AND GET /diet/plan both fold ad-hoc MealLog rows into the day's consumed totals (nyu_backend backend.py:6851-6893, comment "Fold ad-hoc custom meal logs (MealLog) for the day into consumed totals" -> calories_consumed). But the DASHBOARD diet card is computed from a DIFFERENT source: diet_summary.progress = {current: diet_completed_today, target: diet_target_today}, both func.count(AssignedMeal.id).join(UserDietPlan) (backend.py:3481-3494, 3684-3689). A no-plan user has no UserDietPlan/AssignedMeal -> target=0, current=0, and the card NEVER reads MealLog. The frontend derives dietHasPlan = diet_summary.progress.target > 0, so it renders the "No diet plan yet / Generate diet plan" empty state.

CustomMealModal invalidates ['dashboard-overview'] after logging (CustomMealModal.tsx:371), but because the dashboard's data source ignores MealLog, that refetch changes nothing.

Repro:
1. No-plan user -> /nutrition -> log 2-3 meals via the diary (use the photo or Ingredients path so they carry kcal).
2. /nutrition diary shows "Today's food diary · N items · NNNN kcal logged".
3. Go to Dashboard.
Expected: the dashboard diet card acknowledges the logged food (a "logged N meals / NNNN kcal today" state), not a dead "no plan" prompt.
Actual: Dashboard diet card shows "No diet plan yet / Generate diet plan" — zero acknowledgment; the diary and the home surface disagree.

[bug-hunt] Fasting is tracked in TWO independent, unsynchronized systems, so the app shows contradictory "am I fasting?" state and a fast started in one surface is invisible in the other.

System A (older, nutrition-embedded): src/pages/Nutrition.tsx FastingBanner + a per-day 16:8 elapsed timer keyed on localStorage `nyus_fast_start_${todayLocal()}` (Nutrition.tsx:66, 306-311) PLUS the backend fasting-DAY flag from getFastingStatus GET /daily-logs/fasting (nutrition.service.ts:107, useNutritionData.tsx:328). This drives the FastingBanner + the meal-list overlay.

System B (new V1, closes i-20260708-fst1, commit 70a395c8): src/hooks/useFasting.ts + src/lib/fasting.ts, keyed on a completely different localStorage store `nyus_fasting_active` / `nyus_fasting_history`, with NO backend call at all. This drives the Dashboard Fasting card (DashboardFastingCard.tsx) and the /fasting detail page.

The two share NOTHING -- different localStorage keys, and B never touches the backend fasting-day. So:
- Start a 16:8 fast on the Dashboard card or /fasting -> nyus_fasting_active is set, a live timer runs. Open Nutrition -> FastingBanner shows nothing (it reads nyus_fast_start_* + the backend day-flag), and the meal-list behaves as a normal (non-fasting) day. The fast the user just started has zero effect on their meal plan / calorie framing / streak / coach.
- Conversely, mark today a fasting day in Nutrition (backend flag) or run the nutrition 16:8 timer -> the Dashboard Fasting card still reads 'Track your eating window / Start a fast' (idle), because it only knows about nyus_fasting_active.

Repro:
1. Dashboard -> Fasting card -> 'Start 16:8'. Card shows a live count-up.
2. Navigate to /nutrition. No fasting banner; meals fully interactive as a normal day.
3. (reverse) In /nutrition mark today a fasting day -> back to /dashboard -> Fasting card still shows idle 'Start a fast'.

Expected: one source of truth for the user's fasting state; starting/ending a fast in any surface is reflected everywhere (and ideally informs the meal overlay / streak).
Actual: two disjoint 16:8 timers + a backend day-flag that don't know about each other -> contradictory state, and a Dashboard/​/fasting timer that is purely cosmetic (no impact on nutrition, streak, or coach).

Fix (owner decision on scope): unify on a single fasting source of truth -- either back the V1 timer with the same backend fasting-day + nyus_fast_start_* the nutrition banner uses, or have both surfaces read/write one shared module. At minimum the Dashboard/​/fasting timer should reflect (and set) the same 'fasting today' state the Nutrition page uses so the app never shows two contradictory fasting states at once.

[bug-hunt] Dashboard: CoachIntakeCard submits untouched slider/emoji DEFAULT values as if they were real answers -> feeds the coach fabricated baselines and never re-asks.

Root cause (src/pages/_components/dashboard/CoachIntakeCard.tsx + src/lib/coach-intake-questions.ts + src/hooks/useCoachIntake.ts). `values` is seeded from each question's defaultValue (CoachIntakeCard.tsx:164-179). The Save-enable gate hasAnswer = questions.some(q => q.toPayload(values[q.key]) != null) (lines 183-186) runs values through toPayload, but for numeric kinds (emoji/clock/slider) toPayload is the identity (v)=>v (coach-intake-questions.ts ~131/143) and the seeded value is a number, so != null is ALWAYS true. The purple Save button is therefore enabled from mount with zero interaction, and handleSave -> submit(values) writes every default to /profile/extended-intake, then marks the pair answered so the drip never re-asks.

The first deferred pair for a fresh user is stress_level (emoji, default 5) + baseline_sleep_hours (clock, default 7) -- both numeric -- so it triggers on the very first showing.

Repro:
1. Fresh user, 2nd dashboard visit of the day -> Coach intake card appears ('<coach> wants to get to know you').
2. Do NOT move any slider. Tap the prominent purple 'Save' button (natural way users dismiss the card).
Result: stress_level=5 and baseline_sleep_hours=7 persist as the user's REAL baseline; coach is fed fabricated data and never re-asks. A user whose real stress is 9 / sleep is 5h ends up with silently-wrong health data.

Expected: only deliberately-set values persist; untouched numeric questions count as blank (Save disabled until a real interaction, OR untouched values omitted from the payload).

Fix: track a 'touched' set (or seed numeric values as undefined and let QuestionControl render defaultValue for display only via its existing typeof-value-is-number ? value : defaultValue fallbacks), then have hasAnswer + submit treat untouched numeric questions as blank. Watch the values-reset effect (line 180) and the hook submit payload mapping -- real regression surface, so QA the whole intake drip after the change.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Live workout player declares a set the "final set" based purely on set NUMBER, not on whether all target sets were actually logged. In ExerciseWheelPicker.handleLogSet (src/components/ExerciseWheelPicker.tsx:341) it fires onSetComplete(true) whenever setData.set_number === targetSets, with no check that sets 1..targetSets-1 were logged. Activity.handleSetComplete (src/pages/Activity.tsx:672) then advances to the next exercise or declares the whole workout done. Two demonstrable symptoms from the same root cause:

(A) OUT-OF-ORDER LOG -> premature completion. Repro: open an exercise whose target is 3 sets (e.g. 3x8-10), tap the Set 3 row to activate it, and log it FIRST (reverse-pyramid / top-set-first is common for the strength persona this app targets). Expected: nothing special; sets 1-2 still pending. Actual: onSetComplete(true) fires -> if more exercises remain, the "Set complete - Next up" banner pops prompting the user to move on; if this is the last exercise, "Workout complete" + confetti + completion sound fire with only 1 of 3 sets logged.

(B) EDIT-AFTER-COMPLETE -> celebration replays. Repro: log all 3 sets of the LAST exercise normally (workout-complete banner shows, confetti + sound fire once - correct). The picker stays mounted/open above the banner. Tap the already-logged Set 3 row -> the editor expands -> tap "Update". Expected: a silent value update. Actual: handleLogSet runs again with set_number === targetSets -> onSetComplete(true) -> Activity.handleSetComplete else-branch unconditionally re-runs setShowWorkoutCelebration(true) + playCompleteCue(), so the confetti overlay and completion sound REPLAY on every edit of the final set.

Fix: gate completion on distinct logged target sets covering 1..target_sets (count reached), not on set_number equality; and skip re-firing the celebration when showWorkoutComplete is already true.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Profile: avatar upload will silently drop the image file (sends empty JSON {"file":{}} instead of multipart form-data). This is a REGRESSION of the fix for i-20260704-a0ec, which over-corrected.

Root cause (frontend):
- The shared axios instance is created with an instance-level default header Content-Type: application/json (src/lib/api-client.ts:12-13).
- The avatar upload (src/pages/_components/profile/ProfileIdentityCard.tsx:130-132) builds a FormData, appends "file", and does apiClient.post("/users/me/avatar", formData) with NO per-request Content-Type override.
- Commit 98386822 (i-20260704-a0ec) REMOVED the previous "Content-Type: multipart/form-data" override, reasoning "let axios set it automatically." But that only works when there is no instance default forcing JSON. Because the instance default is application/json, axios 1.x transformRequest (node_modules/axios/lib/defaults/index.js) sees a JSON content-type on a FormData body and runs formDataToJSON -> serializes it to the string {"file":{}} and sends Content-Type: application/json. Verified by running the repo axios with the identical instance config: body = {"file":{}}, no multipart, no boundary, binary gone.

Why latent today: the backend /users/me/avatar endpoint does not exist yet (404s) and the catch masks it as a "Photo saved locally" toast. So no current user impact -- but the moment the backend avatar endpoint ships, uploads will fail server-side (empty JSON, no file) with no error surfaced to the user.

Correct fix: neither the removed "multipart/form-data" (breaks because axios/XHR will not append the boundary when you set the header manually -- the original i-20260704-a0ec concern) NOR the current bare post (JSON default). Set the per-request header to undefined so axios deletes the JSON default and the browser generates "multipart/form-data; boundary=...":
  apiClient.post("/users/me/avatar", formData, { headers: { "Content-Type": undefined } })
Ship this together with the backend endpoint so it can be verified end-to-end. Same pattern would bite any future FormData upload on this instance (e.g. ProgressPhotos, support attachments) -- audit those when fixing.
